title: Extensionality of prime-factor sets for Mval move-invariance (IMO 2026 Q1)
intent: Prove the invariant Mval B = Mval B' for a single move, by first identifying the two index finsets B.prod.primeFactors and B'.prod.primeFactors by extensionality (ext p), then matching the products termwise with Finset.prod_congr and gExp_move.

parent.name: Mval_move
parent.statement: theorem Mval_move {B B' : Board} (h : Move B B') (hB : ∀ a ∈ B, 0 < a) (hB' : ∀ a ∈ B', 0 < a) : Mval B = Mval B'

children.name: hset
children.closed_by: ext p; rw [mem_primeFactors_iff_gExp hB, mem_primeFactors_iff_gExp hB']; constructor; both directions by gExp_move hp h

children.name: Mval_termwise
children.statement: ∏ p ∈ B'.prod.primeFactors, p ^ gExp p B = ∏ p ∈ B'.prod.primeFactors, p ^ gExp p B'
children.closed_by: Finset.prod_congr rfl; intro p hp; rw [gExp_move hpp h] (hpp : p.Prime recovered from hp)

applicability.goal_shape: an equality f B = f B' where f is a product (or sum) over an index finset that depends on B, e.g. ∏ p ∈ S(B), term p B
applicability.use_when: the index finsets can be shown equal by extensionality via a shared membership characterisation, and the summed term is invariant under the step
applicability.avoid_when: the index-set equality is not literally true; the membership characterisation is itself the hard part; or the summed term depends on the index set beyond the index variable

consequences: ext p creates a two-way membership obligation (an iff); here both directions close by gExp_move, but in general they may need different arguments. The product step needs a plain equality of index sets for rw [hset], and the summed function must be pointwise invariant. Reaching for Finset.prod_congr before identifying the index sets leaves a goal over two different finsets that prod_congr cannot compare.
